system.name: Nu
system.one_liner: a runtime that decomposes application state into proclets so resources can be reassigned across machines at microsecond scale

content.subject: how one proclet migrates from Machine 0 to Machine 1 while other proclets in the same logical process stay put

summary: This figure shows Nu's core migration mechanism for logical processes. Two machines each run a runtime layer hosting one or more logical processes, which are themselves collections of proclets, fine-grained partitions of program state drawn as a heap circle with thread squiggles. Machine 0 hosts Logical Process A and part of Logical Process B; Machine 1 hosts the rest of Logical Process B. A dashed, ghosted circle inside Machine 0's Logical Process B group marks a proclet's old position, and a curved blue arrow labelled 'Migration' traces its move to a solid circle in Machine 1's Logical Process B group. Because a proclet already bundles its own heap and threads, relocating it between machines needs no special migration protocol beyond moving that self-contained unit, letting Nu reassign resources at microsecond scale.
summary_zh: 该图展示Nu的迁移机制：机器0上逻辑进程B的一个proclet（堆+线程）以虚线幽灵圆圈标记原位置，经蓝色迁移箭头移动到机器1上实心圆圈的新位置，而进程A及其余proclet保持不变，体现迁移即整体重定位。
notes: Palette hex values come from the index's measured-attributes summary, since no source-SVG colour histogram exists for this figure; colours are matched to the figure by visual inspection. 'Logical Process B' is drawn once in Machine 0 and again in Machine 1 (kept as literal duplicate labels); the migration relation is expressed at the Machine (lane) level to avoid ambiguity.
